nodes.label: Design goal: diagnose superpowers sessions with path:line evidence
nodes.rationale: Ship skills/diagnosing-superpowers, a pure-prose skill that helps a human partner pin down what went wrong in a session, reports what happened with path:line evidence, exports a scrubbed bundle, files a GitHub issue, and searches for similar local sessions.

nodes.label: Architecture: one lean SKILL.md plus prompts/, references/, templates/ with no shipped scripts
nodes.rationale: One lean SKILL.md (workflow, hard rules, Red Flags) plus one file per subagent job under prompts/, per-harness session-store references under references/, and output recipes under templates/. No shipped scripts because the model does the work using jq/python3/shell it already has.

nodes.label: Development process: RED baseline scenarios, GREEN with skill, REFACTOR loopholes
nodes.rationale: Skill content is developed RED -> GREEN -> REFACTOR per superpowers:writing-skills: baseline scenarios first, skill written to the observed failures, re-run, loopholes closed, so the Red Flags table and hard rules are grounded in observed agent rationalizations rather than design hypotheses.

nodes.label: Constraint: field-level claims only for verified harness formats
nodes.rationale: No invented harness formats: field-level claims appear only in references/claude-code-sessions.md (verified against Claude Code 2.1.247 transcripts) and references/codex-sessions.md (verified against Codex CLI 0.147.0 / 0.149.0 rollouts); every other harness goes through the discovery procedure so the report reader can judge inferred layouts.

nodes.label: Constraint: skill prose says 'your human partner', never 'the user'
nodes.rationale: The skill addresses a collaborator, not a customer: keeping 'your human partner' frames the agent as working alongside the person, consistent with superpowers conventions; the structure test enforces it by grepping for 'the user'.

nodes.label: Constraint: SKILL.md description 'Use when' third person, body under 1000 words
nodes.rationale: A trigger-style description without workflow summary keeps SKILL.md a router, not a runbook; the 1000-word body budget is enforced by the structure test so the skill stays lean and quick to load.

nodes.label: Constraint: no machine-specific paths or person names in shipped files
nodes.rationale: Shipped files must be portable: no /Users/ or /home/ paths and no person's name (session UUIDs are fine), so the skill works on any executor's machine; the structure test scans for leaks.

nodes.label: Constraint: session files are never modified, moved, or deleted
nodes.rationale: The transcript is the evidence base: any modification destroys the audit trail that path:line citations point at, so diagnosis must be strictly read-only.

nodes.label: Constraint: human approval before archiving or posting
nodes.rationale: Nothing is archived before the human partner has seen the scrub log and file list, and nothing is posted to GitHub before approval of the exact text, because unapproved export can leak private data and an unapproved issue publicly commits the team to a claim.

nodes.label: Constraint: the skill never names a defect or proposes a change to superpowers
nodes.rationale: The agent reports evidence; whether superpowers needs a change is the triager's call. The single allowed statement is the report's 'Superpowers involvement: not indicated / possible / likely' line with its evidence, which keeps the bundle a neutral evidence pack instead of a self-justifying bug report.

nodes.label: Core principle: every finding cites path:line, no citation no finding
nodes.rationale: Findings without a path:line citation are dropped by the dispatcher, which forces evidence-backed reporting and lets the human partner or a maintainer re-verify every claim against the original files.

nodes.label: Mechanism: context-safety reading of transcripts (counts and line numbers first, then trimmed fields)
nodes.rationale: A single transcript line can be a megabyte, so never cat or grep a transcript for content: check wc -lc and long lines first, get line numbers and counts, then extract small fields from specific lines, to keep the agent's own context from blowing up.

nodes.label: Workspace: ~/.superpowers/diagnosing-superpowers/<session-id>/
nodes.rationale: Per-session workspace directory where the case file, report, and bundle live; the skill prints the path when it creates it and again in the report so the human partner always knows where artifacts are.

nodes.label: Local fixtures: CC-huge, CC-compact, CC-this, CX-big, CX-sub transcripts
nodes.rationale: Five real local transcripts chosen by characteristics (size, max line length, compaction present, subagents present, live session) serve as test fixtures for scenarios; executors on other machines pick equivalents and record the substitution, and fixture paths never ship.

nodes.label: Proposed file structure of skills/diagnosing-superpowers
nodes.rationale: SKILL.md plus CREATION-LOG.md, references/ (claude-code-sessions, codex-sessions, other-harnesses), prompts/ (seven analyst dimensions plus scrub, scrub-audit, similar-session), templates/ (case, report, bundle-README, issue), a bash structure test, and a one-line README entry.

nodes.label: Task 1: eleven RED baseline scenarios dispatched to fresh subagents without the skill
nodes.rationale: Eleven complaint-shaped scenarios (vague/hurried, authority push, huge line, export in a hurry, subagent misdirection, retrieval, too long, extra work, expensive, live session, issue handoff) establish the failure baseline; observed rationalizations are collected verbatim to drive the Red Flags table.

nodes.label: tests/diagnosing-superpowers/test-skill-structure.sh: shell structure test
nodes.rationale: Checks what a shell can check: frontmatter name/description shape, SKILL.md word budget, required sections, referenced files exist, no local paths or names leaked, no 'the user' in prose; behavior is tested by scenarios, so the test stays RED until SKILL.md lands (Task 6).

nodes.label: references/claude-code-sessions.md: Claude Code session store field map and safe extraction
nodes.rationale: Verified against Claude Code 2.1.247: main/subagent transcript locations under ~/.claude/projects, line-type envelope, field map for prompts, tool calls, skill invocation and attribution, tokens, hooks, compaction, plus jq/python3 size-safe extraction recipes.

nodes.label: references/codex-sessions.md: Codex rollout field map and safe extraction
nodes.rationale: Verified against Codex CLI 0.147.0/0.149.0: rollout file layout under ~/.codex/sessions, session_meta/turn_context/response_item/event_msg line types, field map for identity, prompts, tool calls, turn timing, cumulative tokens, compaction, subagent linkage, and jq recipes that never print a whole line.

nodes.label: references/other-harnesses.md: six-step discovery procedure for unverified harnesses
nodes.rationale: For any harness without a verified reference: ask the harness, look under its config directory, confirm a candidate by its first human message, map needed fields, record store path and confidence in coverage notes, and if the store cannot be found ask the human partner instead of guessing another harness's layout.

nodes.label: templates/case.md: case file the controller fills before dispatching analysts
nodes.rationale: Captures the agreed problem statement, session inventory (id, path, lines, bytes, longest line, first prompt), rejected candidates, environment (OS, harness, models, superpowers install root/version/sha, sha1 of skill files read or injected, other plugins), and the context-safety rules every analyst must follow.

nodes.label: templates/report.md: diagnosis report with REQUIRED slots
nodes.rationale: Nine sections, every REQUIRED slot filled or replaced with 'none found - checked: <what>': problem statement, triage verdict with confidence, environment, sessions examined, per-turn timeline, findings for seven dimensions, superpowers involvement (not indicated / possible / likely only), coverage notes, and optional similar-sessions table.

nodes.label: templates/bundle-README.md: README for the export bundle with redaction levels
nodes.rationale: Explains what a scrubbed bundle is (an evidence pack, by design containing no diagnosis of superpowers), lists its files (report, case, environment.json, timeline, findings, condensed transcripts, scrub-log), how to read it via [L<n>] line markers, and the three redaction levels: skeleton, evidence, full.

nodes.label: templates/issue.md: GitHub issue body conforming to the repo bug_report template
nodes.rationale: Follows .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md so created issues satisfy it: environment table, superpowers-vs-platform question, problem statement plus triage verdict with path:line rewritten as transcript line numbers, and an explicit 'this report does not propose a fix' stance.

nodes.label: Common analyst subagent header block (read CASE first, context safety, finding return format)
nodes.rationale: Every analyst prompt starts with the same verbatim header: read the case file first, follow its context-safety rules, 'the current session' is not a thing (only paths in CASE count), and return only findings in the report-section shape with path:line evidence plus a Checked line, so a finding without a citation gets discarded by the dispatcher.

nodes.label: prompts/skill-timeline.md: analyst dimension - skill and plugin timeline, missed/late triggers
nodes.rationale: Builds the per-human-turn record of skill and plugin use: every skill invocation, every non-superpowers plugin/skill/MCP server/hook, and turns whose request matches a skill's trigger description with no invocation (missed) or an invocation only later (late); it reports the match and the absence and leaves the judgment to the reader.

nodes.label: prompts/plan-adherence.md: analyst dimension - recovered plan vs. what happened
nodes.rationale: Recovers the session's commitments (agreed plans, spec files, todo lists), marks structural events between commitment and execution (compaction, resumes, aborts, subagent dispatches), and reports skipped, out-of-order, silently changed, invented, or post-structural-event-drift steps.

nodes.label: prompts/repeated-work.md: analyst dimension - duplicated reads/edits/commands/dispatches
nodes.rationale: Extracts every tool call as (line, turn, tool, key), groups by (tool, key) with count thresholds (>=3 reads/searches, >=2 edits, non-idempotent shell commands, same subagent description twice), distinguishes re-reads after an edit (not a finding) from re-reads after a compaction or with nothing in between, and flags re-derived decisions.

nodes.label: prompts/stumbles.md: analyst dimension - errors, retries, reverts, corrections
nodes.rationale: Finds every point where the session stopped going forward: tool errors, failed shell commands, same-turn retries, reverted edits, assistant backtracking phrases, human corrections, permission denials, hook failures, API errors, rate limits, aborted turns, and mid-task compaction, each with recovery status.

nodes.label: prompts/quality-evidence.md: analyst dimension - tests, claim verification, commits, review handling
nodes.rationale: Judges the process against its own claims without reviewing the code: test runs and what followed failures, 'done/fixed/passing' claims with no supporting tool result in the same turn, commit messages that overstate or omit the preceding work, review points acknowledged but not acted on, and acceptance criteria met/not met/not checked.

nodes.label: prompts/request-conflicts.md: analyst dimension - contradictory human instructions
nodes.rationale: Only human-typed prompts count (not hook output, system reminders, tool results, or a parent agent): reports instructions that cannot both be followed, instructions conflicting with a loaded instruction file, instructions to skip or override a step/skill/rule, and scope-changing clarification answers, without judging who was right.

nodes.label: prompts/cost-and-time.md: analyst dimension - token and wall-clock accounting
nodes.rationale: Accounts for where tokens and wall-clock went: per-human-turn and per-subagent token totals (Codex cumulative events differenced), top-5 largest turns, >10-minute gaps, the ten longest tool-result lines, compaction counts and pre/post tokens, and subagent token/duration breakdowns; findings are concentrations with numbers, no speculation.

nodes.label: prompts/scrub.md: scrubber rewrites the bundle in place and writes scrub-log.md
nodes.rationale: Replaces emails, people, org identifiers, secrets, hosts, home paths, repositories (unless public), and proprietary terms with stable numbered placeholders (<EMAIL-n> etc.) applied consistently across every file in the bundle, writes a scrub-log of placeholder -> category -> count without ever writing the original value, and keeps session ids, tool names, skill names, model ids, and line numbers because the bundle is useless without them.

nodes.label: prompts/scrub-audit.md: independent scrub checker returning CLEAN or MISSED
nodes.rationale: A second agent reads every condensed bundle file in full and reports only what the scrubber missed (file:line - category - first 20 characters), never fixing anything and never commenting on quality, so the human partner gets an independent check before archiving.

nodes.label: prompts/similar-session.md: per-candidate signature matcher for similar local sessions
nodes.rationale: Given a diagnosed session's case file, one candidate transcript, and a signature of markers (skill-sequence, error-string, repeated-command, repeated-file, compaction-then, missed-trigger, free), returns match yes/partial/no with per-marker hit/miss/unknown and path:line evidence, enabling the report's similar-sessions section.

nodes.label: Red Flags table in SKILL.md: observed rationalizations vs. reality
nodes.rationale: Rows are design hypotheses that Task 6 edits against CREATION-LOG.md 'Rationalizations observed': keep a row only if a baseline run produced that rationalization (reworded to the verbatim phrase), add rows for uncovered observed rationalizations, and drop rows nothing supports, so the table counters exactly the excuses agents actually make.

nodes.label: Hard rules in SKILL.md: context safety, read-only, exact paths, human prompts only, no diagnosis, approval gates
nodes.rationale: The contract lines of the skill: check sizes before reading and never cat/grep for content, never modify session files, pass absolute paths to subagents, count only human-typed prompts, state superpowers involvement without diagnosing it, and gate archiving and posting on human approval of what they saw.

nodes.label: SKILL.md workflow: intake, locate, triage with seven analysts, report, GitHub issues, export, similar sessions
nodes.rationale: Seven-step workflow with conditional steps 5-7: problem intake one question at a time until a real problem statement exists, locate sessions via the harness references and fill the case file, triage by dispatching one analyst per dimension in parallel (splitting long transcripts by turn range) and discarding uncited findings, then fill the report; GitHub search/draft only on approval, export only with a chosen redaction level and CLEAN audit, similar sessions only when asked.

nodes.label: Quick reference table in SKILL.md: complaint to starting dimension
nodes.rationale: Maps common complaints ('it took too long', 'extra work', 'so expensive', 'what is it doing', 'ignored the plan', 'skill X never fired') to the analyst dimensions to start with, so triage begins on the right track.

nodes.label: Micro-tests: five reps per prohibition, control arm vs. skill arm
nodes.rationale: For each prohibition with an observed baseline violation, run 5 fresh subagents with and without the full SKILL.md content and tabulate control vs. skill violations /5 plus variance; a prohibition with 0/5 control violations stays a contract line without Red Flags rows, keeping the table evidence-driven.

nodes.label: GREEN re-run of scenarios 1-11 with per-scenario pass criteria
nodes.rationale: The same eleven scenarios are re-run with 'Read SKILL.md first and follow it' prepended, each with concrete pass criteria (asks instead of analyzing, no superpowers fix, no >2000-char transcript content, no archive before scrub log, absolute paths in subagent prompts, exact issue text shown), with responses recorded verbatim and compared to baseline.

nodes.label: Task 7: end-to-end run on fixture CC-compact recorded in CREATION-LOG.md
nodes.rationale: One full run (intake on 'the session repeated work after a compaction', locate, seven analysts, report, evidence-level export with scrub and audit, GitHub search only) verified against a checklist: workspace path printed, all REQUIRED report sections filled, sha1 table present, absolute paths for every transcript, per-turn token totals, bundle CLEAN with no /Users/ leaks, and no fixture file changed.

nodes.label: Redaction placeholder scheme: <EMAIL-n>, <PERSON-n>, <ORG-n>, <SECRET-n>, <HOST-n>, <REPO-n>, <PROPRIETARY-n>
nodes.rationale: Stable numbered placeholders, one per original value, ordered by first appearance within the bundle, so a reader can correlate redacted values across files while never seeing the originals; home paths are rewritten to ~/ and the account-name segment removed.

nodes.label: Commit convention: messages end with the Claude-Session trailer for this branch
nodes.rationale: Every commit in the plan carries 'Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01DyaGKhTXvHNs2JgPhDktz7' so the branch's work stays traceable back to the session that produced it.
